PUNCH Newspapers has won the Print Media Category of the 2026 ReportHer Awards, organised by Women Radio 91.7 and the Wole Soyinka Centre for Investigative Journalism, in recognition of its efforts to advance women’s representation in the media. The newspaper emerged winner at the third edition of the awards, held alongside a media parley in Arepo, Ogun State, on Friday. The awards recognised journalists and media organisations committed to improving the visibility and representation of women and girls in the country’s news coverage. The Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria won the Radio Category, News Central TV emerged winner in the Television Category, while HumAngle clinched the Digital Media Award. Temitope Mustapha won in the Individual Journalist Category for amplifying the voices of women. Speaking at the ceremony, the Chief Executive Officer of Women Radio WFM 91.7 and Executive Director of the Voice of Women Empowerment Foundation, Toun Okewale-Sonaiya, said the awards were founded on the belief that women must not be missing from the country’s stories. She disclosed that the third edition received 311 nominations from journalists and media organisations across the country, from which five winners were selected. Congratulating the recipients, Okewale-Sonaiya said, “You did not just report the news. You reported her. You gave women visibility. You gave women voices. And you gave women value.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Ahead of the 2027 general elections, she noted that only 1,481 (10.1 per cent) of the 14,674 candidates contesting the five major elective offices are women, compared with 89.9 per cent men. The award ceremony followed a media parley organised by Women Radio WFM 91.7 in collaboration with the Voice of Women Empowerment Foundation under the Renewed Women’s Voice and Leadership Nigeria programme, themed Advancing Women’s Representation Through Gender-Responsive Journalism. At the parley, journalists and editors called for more deliberate efforts to amplify women’s voices, particularly those making significant contributions at the grassroots. ‘May–July registrants to get PVCS in Dec’ INEC tests result transmission network for 2027 polls today Kaduna seeks clerics’ support for APC Veteran journalist and Women’s Editor at The Sun, Josephine Uba, urged media organisations to look beyond prominent women and profile those whose contributions to their communities often go unnoticed. “We need to focus more on women at the grassroots,” Uba said, noting that women in rural communities play significant roles in raising families, running businesses, and contributing to society. Women’s Editor at Vanguard, Morenike Taire, urged journalists to be patient when seeking interviews with women, noting that some are reluctant to speak for fear of public criticism, making mistakes, or being quoted out of context. She recommended conducting interviews in languages women are comfortable with and providing interpreters where necessary. Participants also called on journalists to challenge gender stereotypes in their questions and reports, particularly when covering women seeking political office or occupying leadership positions. They argued that women should not be defined by their marital status or routinely asked how they intend to combine public responsibilities with family life. Speaking at the parley, the Deputy Editor of PUNCH’s Weekend Titles, Tessy Igomu—who represented the newspaper’s Managing Director and Editor-in-Chief, Dr Adeyeye Joseph—emphasised the importance of improving women’s visibility in media coverage. Tolulope Adeleru-Balogun, Director of Programmes at News Central Media Limited, who represented the Managing Director and Editor-in-Chief of News Central TV, Kayode Akintemi, said editors play a critical role in determining whose voices are heard and whose experiences become part of the national conversation. Citing the 2025 Global Media Monitoring Project, the participants noted that women account for only 26 per cent of people appearing as news subjects and sources in global print and broadcast news. They stressed that gender-responsive journalism does not mean lowering editorial standards or granting women preferential treatment, but ensuring they have a fair opportunity to be heard. Media representatives at the parley pledged to increase their coverage of women, particularly female political aspirants ahead of the 2027 general elections. The organisers said participating media organisations will be encouraged to track their progress and report on the impact of their commitments at the next edition. Temitope Adetunji Temitope Adetunji is a journalist at Punch Newspapers who specialises in human-interest storytelling. She brings years of experience in online journalism into her work, having transitioned into print reporting with a strong digital foundation. Temitope is passionate about amplifying real-life narratives and highlighting the lived experiences that shape everyday people. Her reporting reflects hands-on newsroom experience, empathy-driven storytelling, and a commitment to accurate, people-centred journalism.
